items.value: five arrows in a vertical column, the target at the center of the screen, each 0.7 deg with 0.4 deg between arrows
items.quote: Each stimulus array contained five arrows (>) displayed vertically, with the central (target) arrow in the center of the screen.
items.quote2: each arrow subtended .7 degree of visual angle, with .4 degree separation between the arrows

items.value: congruent (flankers face the target's direction), incongruent (flankers face the opposite direction)
items.quote: For congruent trials, the flankers faced the same direction as the target, whereas for incongruent trials the flankers faced the opposite direction.
Each block of trials had an equal number of left and right targets, and congruent and incongruent stimuli.
Participants completed 48 practice trials followed by 8 blocks of 96 trials.
items.note: 8 x 96 = 768; 384 per condition, as half of each block is congruent.

items.note: Each block had equal numbers of left and right targets and of congruent and incongruent stimuli; the order of trials is not described. 'In random order' in Experiments 2 and 3 refers to the order of block types, not trials.

items.note: The number analyzed is not stated. Table 1 lists 9,486 congruent and 9,471 incongruent observations (18,957), fewer than 25 x 768 = 19,200 trials less the 'less than .9%' trimmed (at least 19,027), so the counts do not settle whether all 25 were analyzed.
No rule for excluding participants is given, and no exclusion is reported; the bootstrap draws 'a sample of size N ... (where N is the number of participants in the experiment)'.

states: 25 recruited; one session of about 40 min; five arrows in a vertical column, each 0.7 deg and 0.4 deg apart, at about 25 inches; congruent and incongruent, equal in each block; 48 practice trials, then 8 blocks of 96 (768); stimulus uncued and until response, no deadline, 350 ms blank screen before the next trial; / and z keys; no error feedback; RTs below 300 ms or above 1500 ms dropped; diffusion models fit by SIMPLEX chi-square minimization
unstated: trial order and its seed, the presentation software, a rule for excluding participants (and the number analyzed), the analysis software
notes: Experiment 1's own Method (5.1.1: Procedure, Stimuli, Participants) holds every stated value except the RT cutoffs, which are in its Results; later experiments refer back to it, not the reverse. PMC's text marks its paragraphs as introduction, but they sit under '5.1.1 Method'. Judgment calls: (1) fixation is read as stated (none) from 'presented uncued ... followed by 350 ms of blank screen until the next trial'; if 'uncued' is not taken to rule out a fixation point, it becomes unstated. (2) responseDeadline and missedResponse are read as stated from 'remained on screen until a response was given'. (3) The number analyzed is not stated (Analyzed (count unstated)), and the observation counts in Table 1 do not settle it. (4) feedback: no error feedback is stated; block feedback is not mentioned. Bibliographic metadata: the PMC record of this author manuscript gives the year as 2012 and the third author as 'Jeffrey S.'; the bibtex uses 2011 (Cognitive Psychology 63(4), as in the paper's references.bib) and 'Jeffrey J.'; the journal name is not in the article text and comes from the DOI.
